name: Bharatanatyam
era_origin: Codified from ancient temple traditions (~2nd century CE text Natya Shastra); revived in its modern form in the early 20th century
costume: Silk sari pleated into a fan shape, temple jewelry, ghungroo bells on the ankles
key_movements: Fixed geometric postures (aramandi/half-sitting stance), intricate hand gestures (mudras), highly expressive facial storytelling (abhinaya)
famous_for: Storytelling through mudras and facial expression; roots in South Indian temples
fun_fact: One of the oldest classical dance forms in the world, originally performed by temple dancers known as devadasis.

name: Kathak
era_origin: Ancient storytelling tradition ('Katha' = story), refined and formalized in Mughal royal courts
costume: Flowing skirt (lehenga) or Mughal-style anarkali; ghungroo ankle bells
key_movements: Fast spins (chakkars), intricate rhythmic footwork synced to tabla, expressive storytelling gestures
famous_for: Rapid spins and intricate footwork perfectly synced to percussion
fun_fact: Kathak performers ('Kathakars') were originally wandering storytellers who used dance and mime to narrate epics.

name: Odissi
era_origin: Ancient temple dance tradition, with references dating back over 2,000 years
costume: Silver filigree jewelry and silk sari with temple-inspired motifs
key_movements: Tribhangi (three-bend body posture), fluid torso movements, sculpture-like poses
famous_for: Sculpturesque poses that mirror ancient temple carvings
fun_fact: Many Odissi poses are directly inspired by stone carvings on temples like the Sun Temple at Konark.

name: Kuchipudi
era_origin: Developed as a dance-drama tradition around the 17th century
costume: Sari and jewelry similar to Bharatanatyam, with distinct regional draping
key_movements: Quick footwork, theatrical dance-drama storytelling; a signature piece is danced on the rim of a brass plate
famous_for: Its dance-drama roots and the plate dance (tarangam)
fun_fact: Traditionally, Kuchipudi was performed only by Brahmin men, who also played the female roles, until the 20th century.

name: Manipuri
era_origin: Ancient dance tradition closely tied to Vaishnavite devotional practice
costume: Elaborate cylindrical skirt (potloi) for the Ras Lila repertoire
key_movements: Gentle, flowing circular movements with minimal sharp angles or heavy footwork
famous_for: Ras Lila performances depicting the divine love of Radha and Krishna
fun_fact: Unlike most classical forms, Manipuri deliberately avoids sharp, percussive movement in favor of soft, continuous flow.

name: Kathakali
era_origin: Developed around the 17th century from temple ritual theatre
music_style: Kerala temple music with Carnatic influences
costume: Elaborate, brightly colored makeup and headgear that identify each character (gods, demons, heroes)
key_movements: Highly stylized eye and eyebrow movements, vigorous footwork, codified hand gestures
famous_for: Elaborate makeup/costume and enacting scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata
fun_fact: The makeup for a single performer can take several hours to apply before a show even begins.

name: Bhangra
era_origin: Centuries-old harvest festival dance
music_style: Punjabi folk, driven by the dhol
costume: Colorful turban (pagri), kurta, and lively accessories
key_movements: High-energy jumps, shoulder shrugs, energetic footwork
famous_for: High-energy celebration at weddings and the harvest festival Baisakhi
fun_fact: Bhangra began as a dance performed by farmers celebrating a good harvest season.

name: Garba
era_origin: Traditional dance performed during the Navratri festival
costume: Colorful mirror-work skirts (chaniya choli)
key_movements: Circular group formations around a central lamp or idol, clapping, rhythmic steps (with sticks in the related Dandiya Raas)
famous_for: Circular group dancing performed throughout the nine nights of Navratri
fun_fact: Garba is traditionally danced around a clay lamp called a 'garbo', symbolizing life.

name: Lavani
era_origin: Traditional folk/theatre dance, popularized around the 18th-19th century
music_style: Lavani folk music driven by the dholki
costume: Nauvari sari (nine-yard drape) and traditional jewelry
key_movements: Powerful hip and footwork, brisk spins, highly expressive storytelling
famous_for: Its rhythm and expressive power, closely tied to Maharashtrian folk theatre (tamasha)
fun_fact: Lavani was historically performed to boost the morale of tired soldiers, and later became central to Marathi folk theatre.

name: Bihu
era_origin: Traditional dance tied to the Bihu harvest festival
costume: Traditional Assamese attire (mekhela chador for women)
key_movements: Fast hip movements, hand gestures, brisk footwork
famous_for: Celebrating the Assamese New Year and harvest season
fun_fact: Bihu is one of the few Indian folk dances traditionally performed by young men and women together as part of a courtship custom.

name: Ballet
origin_region: Italy (Renaissance courts), formalized in France and later Russia
era_origin: 15th century Italy; developed through the 17th-19th centuries in France and Russia
costume: Tutu, pointe shoes, leotards
key_movements: Pointe work, turnout, precise formal positions (the five basic positions)
solo_or_partner: Solo, partner, and group (varies by piece)
famous_for: Pointe technique and formal structure; iconic works like Swan Lake
fun_fact: Ballet terminology is still taught in French worldwide, dating back to its formalization at the French royal court.

name: Salsa
origin_region: Cuba and Puerto Rico, further developed in New York City
era_origin: Mid-20th century, blending Cuban Son with Afro-Caribbean rhythms
costume: Fitted, flowing outfits that allow free hip movement, often in bright colors
key_movements: Quick hip movements, partner turns and spins, basic step patterns on an 8-count
famous_for: A vibrant social partner-dance culture found in clubs worldwide
fun_fact: The name 'salsa' (meaning 'sauce') reflects the spicy blend of musical influences that created it.

name: Flamenco
era_origin: Emerged around the 18th century from Romani, Andalusian, and Moorish traditions
costume: Ruffled dress (bata de cola) for women; fitted suits for men
key_movements: Percussive footwork (zapateado), expressive arm movements, rhythmic hand clapping
famous_for: Rhythmic footwork and raw emotional expression
fun_fact: Flamenco is recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

name: Hip-Hop
era_origin: 1970s, from Bronx street culture
costume: Casual streetwear, sneakers
key_movements: Freestyle movement including breaking, popping, locking, and body isolations
famous_for: Street-style freestyle movement and battle culture
fun_fact: Hip-hop dance grew alongside hip-hop music and graffiti as one of the four foundational pillars of hip-hop culture.

name: Tango
origin_region: Argentina and Uruguay (Rio de la Plata region)
era_origin: Late 19th century, in the working-class immigrant neighborhoods of Buenos Aires
music_style: Tango music, driven by the bandoneon
costume: Fitted dresses with leg slits for women; sharp suits for men
key_movements: Close embrace, sharp leg flicks (ganchos), dramatic pauses
famous_for: Dramatic close-embrace partner work and improvisation
fun_fact: Tango was originally seen as a dance of the working poor before it became a prestigious global ballroom style.

name: Contemporary
era_origin: Mid-20th century, evolving out of modern dance and ballet
music_style: Highly varied, from classical to experimental/ambient
costume: Minimal, flexible clothing that allows free movement
key_movements: Floor work, fall-and-recovery, fluid transitions, personal emotional expression
famous_for: Blending ballet technique with free, expressive, unstructured movement
fun_fact: Pioneers like Martha Graham and Merce Cunningham helped break away from ballet's rigid rules to create this style.

name: Belly Dance
origin_region: Middle East and North Africa, especially Egypt
era_origin: Ancient roots; formalized as a performance art in the 19th-20th century
music_style: Middle Eastern music with Arabic and Turkish influences
costume: Embellished bra-and-belt sets, flowing skirts or hip scarves with coins
key_movements: Isolated hip movements, shimmies, torso undulations
famous_for: Isolated hip and torso movement technique
fun_fact: In its region of origin, belly dance is also known as 'Raqs Sharqi', meaning 'Oriental dance'.

name: Tap Dance
era_origin: 19th century, blending African and Irish/British step-dance traditions
music_style: Jazz, swing, and other rhythmic music
instruments: The dancer's own metal-tipped shoes act as the instrument
costume: Simple, functional clothing paired with metal-plated tap shoes
key_movements: Rhythmic footwork that creates percussive sound patterns
famous_for: Turning the feet into a rhythmic percussion instrument
fun_fact: Tap shoes have metal 'taps' fitted to the heel and toe specifically to amplify the sound of each step.

name: Breaking (Breakdance)
era_origin: 1970s, as part of hip-hop culture
costume: Athletic streetwear
key_movements: Power moves (spins, freezes), footwork, toprock
famous_for: Acrobatic power moves and dramatic freezes
fun_fact: Breaking became an official Olympic sport at the 2024 Paris Games.

name: Waltz
era_origin: Late 18th century
costume: Formal ballroom gowns and suits
key_movements: Smooth gliding steps, rise and fall, the classic box step pattern
famous_for: Being the foundation of Western ballroom dance, always danced in 3/4 time
fun_fact: The waltz was considered scandalous in the 18th century because, unlike earlier dances, partners held each other in a closed embrace.
